mechanism_narrative: A higher unemployment rate (UNRATE) predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days because it signals economic distress and reduced consumer spending power, lowering corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when UNRATE is above 5.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1.0% signals aggressive monetary easing, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 1.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) below their 12-month moving averages signal a deepening economic contraction, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary easing cycle, a decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as it signals effective policy transmission to the labor market, boosting consumer confidence and spending.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when UNRATE declines > 0.1pp in 1 month during a monetary easing cycle, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime (INDPRO < 95.0), a further decline in industrial production (INDPRO) predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as it signals worsening manufacturing output and reduced corporate profitability.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0 and INDPRO declines > 0.5% in 1 month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A low Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as it reduces the cost of capital for corporations, increasing their present value of future cash flows.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 1.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index level below 215.0 signals disinflation, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as it indicates weak economic activity and potential for further monetary tightening to combat deflationary pressures.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL < 215.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) below their 12-month moving averages signal a severe economic contraction, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
